findings.reason: The protected implementation executes a binary search over the array range [0, N-1], comparing equal-length left and right halves via reader.compareSub. For odd ranges, it leaves the rightmost element unpaired; if the two equal halves have equal sums, the unpaired element is the answer. The search uses at most ceil(log2(500000)) = 19 queries, strictly within the 20-call limit, in O(log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space; no candidate is required.

Because all non-exceptional values are identical, comparing equal-length subarrays cancels all common values, so a positive result proves the larger value is in the left subarray, a negative result proves it is in the right, and 0 (for odd ranges) proves it is at the unpaired rightmost index. Halving the search space on each query guarantees convergence.

Each comparison cuts the search interval in half using O(1) work. For N <= 500,000, the maximum query count is 19 (<= 20). Auxiliary space is O(1) as only interval boundary variables are maintained. Complexity evidence is certified and hash-bound.
Accepts an ArrayReader object, respects the 20-query limit, and returns the zero-based index of the unique larger integer.

The approach accurately details comparing equal-length candidate halves, handling even vs odd ranges, halving until 1 index remains, and proving O(log N) query and time bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover linear adjacent comparisons, unequal subarray errors, two elements, odd counts, boundary exceptions, and maximum length bounds.
